en: The Viśveśvarāṣṭaka (The Octave on the Lord of the Universe)

Worship Viśvanātha, the Lord of the city of Vārāṇasī, whose mass of matted hair is as beautiful as the waves of the Gaṅgā, whose left side is perpetually adorned by Gaurī, who is beloved by Nārāyaṇa, and who removes the intoxication of the god of love. Worship him whose nature consists of immeasurable qualities beyond the reach of words, and whose footstool is honored by the gods, Viṣṇu, and Vāgīśa.
...Vārāṇasī [is] with her husband, bearing the weight of a body on her left side.

...Vārāṇasī [is] free from defects such as passion, possessing love for excellent virtues, the abode of dispassion and peace, accompanied by Girijā, the repository of sweetness and fortitude, and delightful even to poison.

Vārāṇasī is the primordial deity, consisting of light, both with parts and partless, non-dual, the root of bliss, unconquered, immeasurable, manifold in nature, possessing attributes and yet devoid of them...
[4] ...the lord of beings, whose limbs are adorned by the foremost of serpents, who wears a tiger-skin garment, has matted hair, and possesses three eyes.
Vārāṇasī is that which holds in its hand the noose, the goad, the bestower of fearlessness, the boon-granting gesture, and the trident...
5 Having abandoned hope, having avoided the censure of others' wealth, and having restrained attachment to sin within the concentration of the mind;
Vārāṇasī is that which [reveals] the Supreme Lord situated in the center of the heart-lotus, the support... 6
Shining with a crown adorned by the cool-rayed moon, his five arrows destroyed by the fire of his eye-like crescent-moon;
his brilliant ear-ornaments fashioned by the lord of serpents; [the one residing in] Vārāṇasī...
7 ...the lion among those intoxicated by evil, the slayer of elephants and of the foremost of demons and serpents.
Vārāṇasī is the forest fire for the wildernesses of death, grief, and fear. 8.

The person who recites this "Eight Verses on the Tiger" (Vyāghrāṣṭaka) by the Supreme Lord, the Sovereign of the City of Vārāṇasī, shall attain knowledge, prosperity, abundant happiness, and infinite fame, and upon the dissolution of the body, shall obtain liberation. 9.
